title: AnnData Export: current route and a verified API workaround
description: Find the nested exporter, understand the observed missing-metadata failure, and export the real downloaded measurement example through an explicit, checked Python workaround.
objectives: Find AnnData Export inside Measure and identify the source measurements database.
Distinguish a failed GUI export from the verified API workaround without inventing missing metadata.
Compare joined, cell-only and nucleus-only matrices and four missing-value policies.
Reopen saved files and preserve object identities, annotations, source images and provenance.
prerequisite: Use the real downloaded measurement example from Annotate, retaining an untouched measurements.db and its source images. The recording uses spaCR 1.5.0.6 and AnnData in the same Python environment. Download the linked helper beside a COPY of measurements.db; it imports spacr.anndata_export.build_anndata. The unmodified GUI/API writer fails on entirely missing object-typed observation metadata, including unknown voxel calibration. A partial .h5ad is not a valid export. The helper explicitly encodes ONLY all-missing object metadata as empty pandas categoricals; it preserves missingness, does not invent calibration or labels, does not change X for this storage step, and does not repair the GUI. It writes a new destination, reloads and compares all values before accepting it; existing destinations are refused. Six exports were independently checked against SQLite: joined/keep 2341x1136 (400320 missing); cell/keep 2341x261 (28 missing); cell/mean 2341x261 (28 imputed); cell/drop_features 2341x257; cell/drop_objects 2334x261; nucleus/keep 2682x341 (1912 missing). No UMAP, GPU operation, image embedding, AI request, biological validation or publication is claimed. API: spacr.anndata_export.build_anndata and export_anndata. The original GUI failure remains preserved separately.

scenes.narration: Open Measure, then its nested AnnData Export workflow. AnnData stores an object-by-feature matrix together with observation metadata and feature names. This lesson shows the current GUI route, but the demonstrated successful exports use an explicit Python workaround. We are not claiming that the GUI export defect is fixed.

Use a copy of the real downloaded measurements database, not an invented table. Keep its images and original database unchanged. The GUI accepts the project folder; our command-line example takes the measurements database file itself. Disable the optional embedding for this export comparison. Exporting a matrix does not require a GPU.

First observe the unmodified writer failing. Some observation columns contain only missing values with an object data type, which this writer cannot serialize. Unknown voxel calibration is one example. Exit status one and a partial file are not success. Do not replace unknown values with zero or the text None to silence the error.

Download the linked helper and inspect its storage workaround. It uses the real build_anndata function, then encodes only entirely missing object metadata as empty categorical columns. Missing values remain missing; known metadata and the feature matrix are not changed by that encoding. This does not mean that physical calibration is a categorical scientific quantity.

Run the helper with your source database, a new output path, and the keep policy. The joined example has two thousand three hundred forty-one cell rows and one thousand one hundred thirty-six features. Related nucleus and pathogen measurements are aggregated onto cells. Four hundred thousand three hundred twenty missing feature values remain missing, not zero.

For one object's own measurements, add single-table cell and keep the missing values. This file has the same two thousand three hundred forty-one cell rows but only two hundred sixty-one features. Twenty-eight feature values are missing. Compare feature names and row identities, not just file size or the number of columns.

The mean policy is a separate analytical choice, not part of the storage workaround. Here it fills twenty-eight missing feature values using the observed column means. The exported missing-value layer records their original positions. Check that imputation is appropriate for your analysis; a complete matrix is not automatically a better or unbiased dataset.

The drop-features policy removes columns containing missing values. In this example four columns are removed, leaving two hundred fifty-seven features and every cell row. Inspect which measurements were removed and why. This policy changes the feature set and can discard useful information; it is not a universal cleaning recommendation.

The drop-objects policy instead removes rows containing missing feature values. Seven cells are removed here, leaving two thousand three hundred thirty-four rows and all two hundred sixty-one features. Missingness can be related to phenotype, acquisition or segmentation. Check what was excluded before treating the retained cells as representative.

Choose single-table nucleus for one row per nucleus, rather than aggregated nucleus features on cell rows. This example has two thousand six hundred eighty-two nuclei and three hundred forty-one features. Keep the parent links and object identities. More nuclei than cells does not mean that extra cells appeared during export.

Reopen each saved file. The helper compares the full matrix, ordered object and feature identities, missingness, and observation metadata; independent SQLite checks also passed for all six files. Annotations remain metadata, not training features inserted into the matrix. Images are not embedded, so retain the source files and their paths with the export.

Use a new output name for each policy and keep the script, settings and package versions. The helper refuses an existing destination instead of overwriting it. These checks establish data preservation for this example, not biological validity or a repaired GUI. Return to the linked API and measurement lessons for the surrounding workflow.
